result.summary: Replaces static headers presync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) in chainparams with runtime computation during node startup in PeerManager. The parameter search algorithm is implemented in C++ based on elapsed time since genesis and the minimum chainwork height, allowing the removal of the offline Python parameter generation script.
result.problem: Release maintainers currently have to run an offline Python script during release preparation and guess the supported lifetime of the software to precompute static sync parameters. These hardcoded parameters gradually drift from optimality as the software ages, and the Python tool's attack model had a flaw that failed to account for an attacker stopping mid-batch.
evidence: Description points out maintainer burden and risk: 'Less work for maintainers that need to occasionally run the current contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py script... Less room for mistakes in that process... Automatically adapts based on time'.

Description and commit message note a modeling flaw in the prior tool: 'The old Python code... actually got it (slightly) wrong by missing the fact that attackers are capable of strategically deciding to stop the attack in the middle of a batch (found by darosior).'
doc/release-process.md removes the manual step of running the script and updating chainparams.
result.scope_notes: Much of the diff is the mathematical search algorithm in src/headerssync.cpp along with fuzz targets and 50 precomputed test cases in src/test/headerssync_tests.cpp.
result.changed_since_previous: No structural changes to the approach; the core migration to runtime optimization and deletion of the devtool remain intact.
result.card: This pull request replaces static headers presync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) with runtime calculation during node startup. Previously, release maintainers had to manually run an offline Python script to guess the software's active lifespan and embed static values in chainparams, which caused parameters to drift from optimality over time and carried an attack modeling flaw regarding mid-batch aborts. The offline tool is deleted and replaced with a closed-form C++ solver, validated by unit test vectors against exhaustive search optima and dedicated fuzz targets. There are no dependencies.

risk.why: A bug in parameter computation could select weak commitment periods or buffer sizes, leaving nodes vulnerable to memory exhaustion or DoS during headers presync.
